title: Thorium fuel cycle demonstration gap
bottleneck: Thorium is abundant and its fuel cycle promises less long-lived waste and inherent proliferation resistance, but no thorium reactor has ever operated commercially. The chemistry of thorium molten salts, protactinium separation, and U-233 handling were demonstrated only at lab scale in the 1960s and 70s. Decades of advocacy have not produced a demonstration plant.
why_it_blocks: Thorium remains a paper fuel cycle. Without an operating demonstration, its claimed advantages are unvalidated and utilities will not adopt it; advocacy without hardware changes nothing. Uranium-233 bred from thorium is weapons-usable, which complicates the proliferation narrative thorium advocates promote, and handling protactinium-233 adds radiological challenges absent from uranium fuel cycles.
current_state: India, China, and private startups have thorium programs. China's thorium molten-salt test reactor is the furthest along, with commercial claims unproven.
